name: Durbar Square (Historic Core)
tagline: The royal heart of the old city
description: The former palace square is Bhaktapur's grand centerpiece, ringed by temples, the 55-window palace, and open brick plazas. Staying nearby puts you steps from the heritage core, with cafes, guesthouses, and endless carved detail, though it is the busiest, most visited pocket.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want to live inside the heritage
pros: Iconic temples and palace on your doorstep

name: Taumadhi Square (Nyatapola)
description: Taumadhi is dominated by the towering Nyatapola temple, Nepal's tallest pagoda, and the nearby Bhairavnath temple. Rooftop cafes here serve juju dhau with a direct view of the climbing temple steps, making it one of the most atmospheric spots to sit, work briefly, and watch daily life.
bestFor: Cafe sitters and temple lovers wanting the best views
pros: Front-row views of the Nyatapola pagoda

name: Pottery Square / Dattatreya Square
tagline: Where clay and old wood meet
description: This eastern quarter blends Pottery Square, where potters still shape and dry clay in the open, with the ancient Dattatreya Square and its famous carved Peacock Window. Quieter and more residential than the center, it offers a working, lived-in feel and some of the city's most authentic craft.
bestFor: Slow travelers drawn to craft and everyday Newari life

name: Nagarkot (Valley Rim)
description: About an hour uphill from Bhaktapur, Nagarkot is a ridge-top escape famed for sunrise Himalayan panoramas on clear days. Cooler, greener, and quieter than the valley floor, it makes an easy overnight for cleaner air, mountain views, and short hikes, then a quick return to the old city.
bestFor: Nature breaks, clear air, and Himalayan sunrises
pros: Panoramic Himalayan views on clear days
Cleaner, cooler air than the valley
cons: Removed from city life and cafes
